standard_prerequisites.reference: Semisimple complete reducibility, Schur lemma, highest weights, quasi-split twists and connecting map, definitions135–173
standard_prerequisites.use: Endomorphism algebras commute with scalar extension; dominant weights can be shifted into the root lattice; the star action has finite image. The current descent and common-field argument must be proved.

standard_prerequisites.name: Brauer theory over Q, R and C
standard_prerequisites.reference: Classical central-simple algebra theory; Tits1971 as used393–406 and921–945
standard_prerequisites.use: R division algebras with these centers are R/C/H; H tensor H is Brauer trivial, quaternion classes have order2, a central division algebra is determined by its Brauer class, and Tits classes add with central characters. No semisimple compatibility criterion is included as an input.

core_obligations: Prove the equivalence between R-universality, preservation of irreducible rational representations after real extension, and Tits division-algebra preservation.
Force all nontrivial star actions to have a common imaginary quadratic inner field and coincide with real conjugation.

Use weights supported on different simple factors to detect quaternion-class cancellations and prove equality of all nontrivial invariant Tits classes. Use an outer nonfixed weight to force splitting of inner-factor Tits algebras over the common field; check the compressed converse for every global dominant weight without granting it as background.

proof_roadmap.step: Pass from arbitrary real representations to unique irreducible highest-weight forms, then use endomorphism division algebras.
A generic star-orbit weight detects the minimal inner field via the center; real division forces an imaginary quadratic field, and root-lattice shifts identify the two star actions.
A single factor representation and sums of invariant factor weights force conditions1–3 through quaternion cancellation.

Mixed weights detect the common-field splitting requirement. For sufficiency, apply the same Tits character/center calculus to fixed and nonfixed global weights, keeping the common-field and outer-factor splitting obligations visible.

The retained local reduction and the all-weight converse are part of the solution. This coordinated Galois/Brauer obstruction analysis exceeds a routine qualifying-exam calculation; no H3 is claimed, and the reader must assess the author compressed converse explicitly.
